newsitem.title: USA: Christian Coalition reports record fundraising.
newsitem.headline: Christian Coalition reports record fundraising.

text.p: The Christian Coalition, a powerful conservative pressure group that helps Republicans, reported Tuesday it raised nearly $27 million in 1996, a 36 percent increase over the previous year.

The Coalition raises money from an estimated 1.3 million grassroots members. Officially non-partisan, it has become one of the most influential groups in the Republican Party with its platform of traditional social values and opposition to abortion.
Much of its funds were spent on distributing 46 million guides for voters in last month's election, using a distribution network of over 126,000 churches.
"Our contributions have skyrocketed and it is clear that 1996 is a record fundraising year for us," said Coalition executive director Ralph Reed.
"Clearly these numbers reflect an explosive momentum at the grassroots level," he said.
Some Democrats have challenged the Christian Coalition's tax-free status, saying it is effectively a Republican political action committee -- a claim the Coalition vigorously denies.
